result.title: PREEN: Exemplar-Based Color Style Transfer with Smartphone Editor Presets
result.summary: We present PREEN (Preset Regression via an Exemplar-based Editor Network), which casts color style transfer as regression onto the 29 parameters of a deterministic image editor. Given a content image and a style reference, PREEN predicts a preset, a vector of editor slider values that is interpretable and editor-consumable, not a raster image. The key obstacle is supervision, since an arbitrary real reference lacks a preset ground truth. We therefore supervise with a style-transfer teacher, whose target looks we invert into the editor's parameter space as pseudo-presets, then pretrain a CLIP-conditioned regressor and refine it with LoRA under an image-level CIELAB loss. On the human-curated PST50 benchmark, PREEN applies the reference's color while preserving structural fidelity, leading the baselines on pixel- and perceptual-fidelity metrics. The preset is compact and predicted at sub-second on-device latency. The low-dimensional subspace also exposes a single inference-time strength knob that traces a continuous default-to-vivid trajectory in one forward pass, with every intermediate state a valid editor preset. A two-axis human study shows that raters prefer the vivid end for matching the reference but the default as a standalone photo, a trade-off the knob spans without retraining.

AI.brief_summary: PREEN 将颜色风格迁移重构为对确定性图像编辑器 29 个参数（preset）的回归：用风格迁移教师模型生成目标外观，反解为伪 preset 作为监督，预训练 CLIP 条件回归器并用 LoRA 与 CIELAB 损失精修，从而输出可编辑、可解释且端上亚秒级的参数向量，并附带一个连续可调的强度旋钮。
AI.relevance_reason: 属图像颜色编辑与参数回归工作，其低维参数空间与插值旋钮服务于图像外观调节，而非 VLM 推理状态生成、视觉证据筛选或停止决策，未见与 LVR 主线的实质联系或可核查的借鉴线索。
